properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:11AM EDT until October 11 at 11:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Buncombe County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Polk County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Rutherford County in western North Carolina...
Northeastern Greenville County in upstate South Carolina...
Northwestern Spartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...

* Until 1100 AM EDT.

* At 511 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of torrential
rainfall training from Glassy Mountain and Gowansville to Tryon,
Columbus, Saluda, Bat Cave, Chimney Rock, and Lake Lure.  This
rainfall will be capable of producing 1-2 inches in less than an
hour.  This rainfall may cause additional rises on area streams,
including the Broad River near Lake Lure and quickly exacerbate
ongoing Minor flooding.  Significant flooding, potentially
impacting some structures, may develop quickly over the next 1-2
hours.  Seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding.  Expect significant
flooding of adjacent low-lying areas, including parks,
trails, low-water crossings, boat-access areas, and
campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and basements
is possible with potential flooding of first-floors in
residences and businesses near streams. Evacuations may be
needed.  An isolated landslide or two cannot be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Columbus, Landrum, Tryon, Lake Lure, Campobello, Saluda, Chimney
Rock Village, Chimney Rock State Park, Bat Cave and Lake Bowen.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

Aho.

http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 11 at 5:24AM EDT until October 11 at 11:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Transylvania County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1115 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 517 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain has recently
departed Transylvania and most of Henderson County. Flooding is
ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the warned area. Between
3 and 6 inches of rain have fallen, but only light additional
rain is expected. Most of the flooding is due to run off from
previous rainfall. Mud Creek in Hendersonville is in Minor Flood,
and still rising.

Common, deeper flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to Mud Creek
is developing with lesser impacts to vulnerable property.  More
significant floodwaters are beginning to impact low-lying areas,
including areas of William H. King Memorial Park and the Oklawaha
Greenway, with inundation approximately 2-4 ft deep.  Secondary
roads and outbuildings may be experiencing flooding up to 1-2 ft
deep.
- Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over
the next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all
evacuation orders from local Emergency Management officials.
Only a few inches of water can strand your vehicle and only 6
inches of water can sweep your vehicle away.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Hendersonville, Brevard, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat Rock,
Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park, Rosman and Dupont State
Forest.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

Carolina...

(English) Broad River At above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling Springs
affecting Cleveland County.

this morning. But runoff from widespread 4 to 6 inches of storm total
rainfall will cause flooding along the Broad River.  Interests all
along the Broad River, even as far upstream as Bat Cave are urged to
monitor river levels and take appropriate action as needed.

* WHERE...(English) Broad River at above Sandy Run Ck, 3 SSW Boiling
Springs.

* WHEN...From this morning to Monday afternoon.

may be approaching the base of residential home foundations between
Abe's Mountain Rd. and the river. At 14.0 feet, Moderate Flood
Stage. Broad River floodwaters may be inundating the foundations of
homes located between Abe's Mountain Rd. and the river and
threatening residential first floors.  Low-lying roads near the
vicinity of Abe's Mountain may be inundated by floodwaters.  The
Broad River Greenway is experiencing flooding of low-elevation
trails and picnic areas along the river.  Floodwaters may be
impacting local campgrounds near the river as well.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 5:30 AM EDT Sunday the stage was 11.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 13.5 feet this evening. It will then
fall below flood stage late tonight.

feet on 01/25/2010.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 11 at 6:29AM EDT until October 11 at 1:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has extended
the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southeastern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Northwestern Burke County in western North Carolina...
West Central Caldwell County in western North Carolina...

* Until 100 PM EDT Sunday.

* At 629 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a line of training cells
producing torrential rainfall entering northwestern Burke and
southeastern Avery counties.  This rainfall will be capable of
producing 1-2 inches in less than an hour over saturated soils.
This rainfall may cause additional, significant rises on area
streams, including the Linville River from Grandfather Mountain to
Linville and Pineola; Wilson Creek near Edgemont; and Warrior Fork
from Jonas Ridge to Table Rock, quickly exacerbating ongoing Minor
flooding.  Significant, Moderate flooding, potentially impacting
some structures and causing significant travel disruptions, may
develop quickly over the next 30-90 minutes.  If you are near a
creek or stream, seek higher ground now!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life-threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams.
Expect significant flooding of adjacent low-lying areas,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat-access
areas, and campgrounds.  Flooding of some crawl spaces and
basements is possible with potential flooding of
first-floors in residences and businesses near streams.
Evacuations may be needed.  An isolated landslide or two
cannot be ruled out.

* Some locations that may experience significant flash flooding
include...
Crossnore, Table Rock, Linville Falls, Lake James State Park, Jonas
Ridge and Edgemont.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.
